text.p: Shares in HSBC Holdings Plc extended recent losses on Tuesday in continued reaction to the strength of sterling and amid talk of increasing mortgage competition in Hong Kong, traders and analysts said.
Traders also said a "sell" recommendation on 61.5 percent owned Hang Seng Bank also weighed on HSBC, which was down 21p at 12.44 by 1158 GMT in volume of 1.1 million shares.
HSBC has dipped after reaching an intraday record of 13.16 stg on November 6, after an extended rally from below 10.00 stg at the end of May.
Bear Stearns Asia earlier said it had started coverage of Hang Seng with a sell rating. "That has just rubbed off on HSBC," said one market maker in the stock.
Analysts and traders said recent downgrades on HSBC, partly to reflect the impact of sterling strengh on the value of its profits, continued to weigh on the shares.
"People have been trimming forecasts and that is just filtering through to the market," said one trader.
Analyst Ian McEwan at Lehman Brothers said there had been vague market talk of increasing mortgage competition in Hong Kong but it was sterling strength which was the key for the shares.
"A strong sterling does weaken the value of profits when expressed in sterling," McEwan said. "That is the only real fundamental reason for the shares to be weak just lately."
Last week, brokerages including ABN AMRO Hoare Govett said they were considering trimming earnings estimates for the bank.
